title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, document per-condition pipeline semantics with explicit archived-artifact references, disclose the protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) offer a pathway to translate operator intent into device CLI, but pose operational risks: syntactic errors, semantic/ordering violations of workflow constraints, and susceptibility to adversarially crafted inputs. Prior prototype work demonstrates benefits when generation is coupled with deterministic validation and repair, yet many evaluations report token- or reference-match metrics rather than deployability or acceptance-for-deployment [3,8,9].

We posed a narrowly scoped operational research question and preregistered its analysis: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The preregistration (cand-2026-03; preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373) fixed a paired confirmatory estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, with shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (single LLM generation per adversarial intent reused by both conditions). This paper reports the executed, artifact-backed experiment and explicitly reconciles natural-language preregistration wording with the registered formal estimand, per reviewer request.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end with archived execution and analysis artifacts; (2) a transparent reconciliation showing the preregistered natural-language H1 (that gating reduces attacker-success) is not supported by the observed formal-estimand outcome; (3) explicit, artifact-grounded pipeline timelines and provider-call accounting that demonstrate shared_initial_candidate reuse; and (4) quantitative outcome, failure accounting, diagnostics for the observed discordant pairs and protocol-deviation disclosure (unset temperature).
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-verification tools such as Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber and VeriFlow have been widely used to check forwarding and configuration invariants and are natural validators for generated configurations [5–7]. Recent NetOps/LLM prototype studies report that LLMs can generate useful drafts but produce syntax/semantic mistakes; coupling generation with verifier feedback and localized repair improves prototype outcomes [3,8]. Surveys of AIOps and telecommunications identify fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally meaningful benchmarks that measure deployability and safety rather than token-level accuracy [4,9]. Security work documents prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks motivating input-sanitization and gating defenses in LLM-integrated systems [10], and tool-augmented orchestration (LLMs calling verifiers/tools then repairing) provides an architectural template for mitigations [11].

Positioning. Our experiment adds a preregistered paired formal-estimand evaluation with shared_initial_candidate semantics so that differences reflect post-generation processing (sanitization, gating, repair) and not differences in initial sampling. We publish per-episode validator traces and deterministic reconciliation so principal numbers are traceable to archived artifacts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. For each adversarial intent we record a binary outcome: 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 would accept the final candidate for deployment, 0 otherwise. Confirmatory inference uses an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Design, task bank and scope. Planned N = 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300 across two conditions). The synthetic intent templates exercise admin, MTU and VLAN operations and constrained required sequences; task generation and adversarial mutation seeds are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Scope is limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded by the validator.

Model, validator and orchestration. Declared generator: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The archived pipeline implemented a generate–validate–repair workflow with a template-based input-sanitizer applied in the guarded branch before gating. Provider-call accounting and stage counts are recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (hosted_model_call_event_count = 156; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and per-condition timeline (artifact-grounded). To address reviewer requests we list the exact per-pair step sequence used in the archived run and cite the concrete reconciliations and counts that demonstrate shared reuse:
1) Task instantiation and adversarial mutation: each pair (task-000001 ... task-000150) is recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl with generation_seed and mutated payload fields. (See representative entry task-000001 in the archive.)
2) Shared initial generation: a single LLM generation call produced a shared_initial_candidate per pair; these are persisted under execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt and the run-level stage_counts record shared_initial_generation = 150. Both Baseline and Guarded scoring artifacts reference this same shared candidate for each pair (evidence: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json show identical shared_initial_candidate_sha256 values).
3) Baseline scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 evaluated the shared_initial_candidate and recorded validation_before and validation_after snapshots in execution/scoring/...-baseline.json.
4) Guarded branch: the pipeline applied template-based input-sanitization prior to gating; sanitized outputs (when changed) are recorded in the task-manifest payload. The verifier gate then accepted or rejected the candidate; when allowed and needed, the pipeline permitted at-most-one automated repair LLM call (repair stage_count = 6). Repair-provider traces (where present) are linked from execution/scoring/...-guarded.json entries.
5) Final validation: validator re-evaluated repaired candidates (or original candidate if no repair) and recorded the guarded final decision and validator trace. Representative per-episode artifacts include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json with validation_before/validation_after objects.

Missingness, exclusions and failure handling. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. Execution manifest and analysis show completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_included = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Both-missing_pairs = 9 were excluded per plan.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider calls. Planned episodes = 300; completed = 282; failed = 18. Model-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 156; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. The primary analysis used 141 complete pairs. Condition totals (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383); guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs are fully traceable: each is associated with repair-stage activity (repair = 6). Per-episode scoring artifacts document validation_before and validation_after snapshots showing that sanitizer or the permitted repair changed command ordering or normalization such that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted the final configuration while the unguarded baseline candidate had failed. Representative artifact chain for one discordant case: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt -> execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (validation_before shows invalid ordering) -> execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (validation_after shows valid normalized configuration).

Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run technical failures and excluded per the preregistered plan (missingness_summary.csv reports both_missing_pairs = 9). A conservative sensitivity mapping both-missing pairs to failures yields baseline acceptance 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance 141/150 = 0.9400; the primary inference remains the preregistered paired McNemar on the 141 complete pairs.

Preregistered but unexecuted items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this archived run; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are available and no claims are made about benign blocking.
sections.discussion:
Hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistration's natural-language H1 stated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker-success (i.e., fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand instead measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These constructs differ: an increase in validator acceptance can indicate successful repair of malformed drafts (operator-labor reduction) rather than enabling attacker success. In our data the guarded pipeline increased validator acceptance by ≈4.255 percentage points because sanitizer/repair recovered reparable drafts that the baseline validator rejected. Therefore the preregistered directional H1 (attacker-success reduction) is not supported by the observed formal-estimand outcome; we report and interpret results with respect to the formal estimand and caution against conflating acceptance-for-deployment with attacker-centric safety without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Operational interpretation and repair–gate trade-offs. Within this synthetic setting, template-based sanitization plus limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that unguarded generation fails to produce. Deterministic gating acts as a safety boundary, but repair policy determines operational effect: repairs enabled acceptance in six discordant pairs. Under differing or weaker validator encodings such repairs could accept semantically unsafe outputs. Thus, co-design of validator coverage, gating rules, and constrained repair scope is necessary for operational deployment.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size; both-run technical failures = 9 were excluded as preregistered. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences and protected-interface invariants but omits some protocol-level dynamic semantics, so acceptance-for-deployment is a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator and synthetic tasks limit generalization across vendors, protocols and production traffic. Conclusion validity: the observed absolute effect is small relative to a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical detectability does not imply broad practical impact.

Reproducibility and protocol deviation. We disclose a protocol deviation: execution/model_configuration.json recorded temperature = null (unset). Because provider defaults can affect sampling, this is a deviation from a fully specified sampling configuration and is recorded in the Disclosure Statement. Paired comparability was preserved in the archived run via shared_initial_candidate semantics (single generation per pair, stage_counts record shared_initial_generation = 150) so both Baseline and Guarded began from an identical initial candidate per pair. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 and re-executing the archived task manifest under identical provider semantics; archived seeds and bootstrap parameters are available (bootstrap_seed = 1729; bootstrap_resamples = 10000).

Recommendations grounded in the archive. (1) Execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or operational reachability checks; (3) diversify generators and validators across vendors and dialects; (4) fix sampling settings (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction. Each recommendation follows directly from archived counts and missingness findings.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Provider-call accounting and per-episode validator traces indicate the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. Crucially, this formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker-success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; execution/model_configuration.json; execution/task_manifest.jsonl).

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
